trial_court: Family Court in HMA Case No. 788/2010
case_name: Jag Parvesh Singh vs Manjeet Kaur
facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties was solemnised on 16.05.2004. They started living separately in a rented accommodation due to temperamental differences and estrangement. Appellant preferred petitions under Section 13 (1) (i-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, which were dismissed as withdrawn.

legal_principles.principle: Procedural sin should never be the death of rights.
legal_principles.held: The processual law so dominates in certain systems as to overpower substantive rights and substantial justice. The humanist rule that procedure should be the handmaid, not the mistress, of legal justice compels consideration of vesting a residuary power in Judges to act ex debito justitiaie where the tragic sequel otherwise would be wholly inequitable.
cited_cases: Kumar Sen Vs. State of Bihar : AIR 1975 SC 1185

legal_principles.principle: Justice is the goal of jurisprudence--processual as much as substantive.
legal_principles.held: While this appeal has to be allowed, for reasons set out impeccably by my learned brother, I must sound a pessimistic note that it is too puritanical for a legal system to sacrifice the end product of equity and good conscience at the altar of processual punctiliousness and it is not too radical to avert a breakdown of obvious justice by bending sharply, if need be, the prescriptions of procedure.
cited_cases: Kumar Sen Vs. State of Bihar : AIR 1975 SC 1185

outcome.final_order: The impugned Ex-parte Judgment/Decree dated 16.07.2013 passed by the Family Court was set aside and the matter was remanded to the trial court.
